source_validation.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.

Interior corridor/office door heights (F1:D1-D6, F2:D1-D6) remain an explicit assumption of 2.1m, matching the elevation-evidenced exterior entrance doors (F1:D7, F1:D8) and confirmed window-head pattern; these 12 interior doors are not directly visible in any supplied elevation (interior partitions are not elevated) and remain unlinked to image height evidence in check_openings.

West wall vestibule/porch recess (~1m deep, corridor width) simplified to a flush exterior wall with a single wide entrance door D7 spanning the corridor width; the small projecting porch geometry itself is not modeled.
South wall small notch/chamfer near the SW entrance simplified to a flush wall with a single door D8.
All door swing/open states left unknown.
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.
No exterior ground-level door assumed on 2F (upper storey); vertical circulation (stair) is not shown in the supplied plan/elevation views and is not modeled.
All door swing/open states left unknown.
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.

unresolved: Vestibule/porch recess geometry on the west facade and the SW corner wall notch are simplified/not modeled as separate enclosed space; only door openings are represented.
Small furniture items (desks, chairs, L-shaped workstation) not modeled; only partitions/openings captured.
Pixel-to-world calibration was supplied by the caller and was not independently verified.
No stair or vertical circulation between F1 and F2 is shown in the supplied drawings; none is modeled.

reused_calibration.basis: 1F: outer wall faces measured to dimension ticks for 15000x8000 overall (matches labeled 15000 and 8000mm chains). Interior partitions at x=5.0m and x=10.0m (piers, from double-line wall support scan) run full building depth. Corridor bounded by two full-width walls at y=5.0m and y=3.0m (from 3000/250/1500/250/3000 mm dimension chain), each with 3 door openings measured from wall-line gaps (pixel profile of wall colour at y=618-629 and y=804-815). South wall of the SW office has a small wall notch/chamfer (~0.3m) around its entrance; simplified to a flush wall with a single door (matches 540/900mm bottom dimension and South elevation door 0-2.1m). Windows measured from cyan hatch band extents on each facade; north/south office windows read from 2400mm-module dimension chain, corridor windows on east/west from 1200mm dimension chain.

claims.reason: North_view.png vertical dimension chain (top to bottom: 800/1800/1000 for the 2F wall zone, then 400/1600/1000 for the 1F wall zone) gives 1F window head/sill. Pixel ticks measured at x~198-214: top=198(z=6.6m, roof line), 2F-window-head=244, 2F-window-sill=347, floor-division(2F level)=405(z=3.0m), 1F-window-head=428(inferred from the 400mm segment after the division; z=2.6m), 1F-window-sill=520(z=1.0m), ground=578(z=0). This one window height family (sill 1.0m/head 2.6m) is used identically on the South, East and West facades (matching East_view.png ticks 174/220/323/381 which reproduce the same 800/1800/1000 and 400/1600/1000 split), so it is applied to all 1F windows regardless of facade.
